competencies.text: Synthesize physics and chemistry principles in real-world applications.

days.title: Putting Physics & Chemistry Together
days.content:
🎯 Learning Target

By the end of today's lesson, you will be able to identify real-world technologies and processes that combine physics and chemistry principles, and explain how they work together to solve everyday problems.

🔬 Why Physics + Chemistry Together?

Physics explains how things move, transfer energy, and interact with forces. Chemistry explains how substances react, bond, and transform. Real-world systems rarely use just one — they combine both.

🧪 Integrated Systems Around You

SystemPhysics ConceptsChemistry Concepts
Car engineTorque, rotational motion, thermodynamicsCombustion of fuel, oxidation reactions
BatteryElectrical current, potential difference, circuitsRedox reactions, electrolytes, ion flow
Air conditionerHeat transfer, fluid pressure, phase changeRefrigerant chemistry, gas laws
Solar panelPhoton energy, electromagnetic wavesPhotovoltaic effect in silicon semiconductors
Water treatmentFluid dynamics, filtrationChlorination, coagulation, pH adjustment
Cooking (frying)Conduction, convection, radiationMaillard reaction, protein denaturation

🔋 Case Study: How a Battery Works

  1. Chemistry: A redox reaction inside the battery releases electrons.
  2. Physics: Electrons flow through the circuit as electrical current.
  3. Result: Current powers devices — from phones to electric vehicles.

Neither physics nor chemistry alone can explain a battery — you need both.

❄️ Case Study: How an Air Conditioner Works

  1. Chemistry: Refrigerant absorbs heat when it evaporates, releases heat when it condenses.
  2. Physics: Compressor raises pressure and temperature; coils transfer heat outside.
  3. Result: Warm room air gets cooled, heat is dumped outside.

🍳 Case Study: Why Cooking Is Physics + Chemistry

  • Physics: Heat travels from pan to food through conduction.
  • Chemistry: Proteins denature, sugars caramelize, and Maillard reactions create flavor.
  • Every meal you cook is a demonstration of both sciences working together.

🏘️ Real-Life Synthesis in the Philippines

  • Rice cookers: Electrical resistance (physics) + water phase change (chemistry).
  • Jeepney engines: Combustion (chemistry) + torque and rotation (physics).
  • Barangay water pumps: Pascal's Principle (physics) + chlorine disinfection (chemistry).
  • Salt beds (asinan): Evaporation (physics) + crystallization of NaCl (chemistry).

💡 The Big Idea

Science doesn't happen in silos. The best solutions to real-world problems — from clean energy to safe food — come from combining physics and chemistry.

📌 Quick Check

  • Why is a car engine both a physics and chemistry system? (Answer: combustion = chemistry; rotation and torque = physics)
  • What chemistry happens inside a battery? (Answer: redox reaction)
  • Name one everyday object that combines physics and chemistry. (Answer: rice cooker, stove, refrigerator, etc.)

days.title: Match Game — Cross-Discipline Applications
days.content:
🔗 Activity 1 — Match the Pairs

Match each real-world system to the correct combination of physics AND chemistry principles it uses. There are 8 pairs and unlimited retakes to reach 75%.

days.title: Scenario Challenge — Integrated Science
days.content:
🎯 Activity 2 — Scenario Challenge

Read each scenario and choose the best reasoning. There are 5 scenarios. You have unlimited retakes to reach 75%.

scenario.text: 🔋 A phone battery gets warm while charging. What combination of physics and chemistry is happening?

choices.label: A) Only electrical physics — no chemistry involved.
B) Chemical redox reactions inside the battery release energy, and electrical resistance (physics) turns some of it into heat.
C) The battery is broken.
D) Only chemistry — the phone's screen heats up the battery.

scenario.text: 🚗 A jeepney burns diesel to move forward. Which set of concepts BEST describes what happens?

choices.label: A) Only chemistry — combustion.
B) Only physics — torque and rotation.
C) Chemistry of combustion releases energy, physics of torque converts that energy into motion.
D) Neither — jeepneys run on batteries.

scenario.text: ❄️ An air conditioner cools a room. What does the refrigerant do?

choices.label: A) It only creates cold air out of nothing.
B) It absorbs heat from inside when it evaporates (chemistry) and releases heat outside when it condenses (physics of pressure and phase change).
C) It removes humidity using magnets.
D) It works purely on electricity — no chemistry involved.

scenario.text: 🍞 When you toast bread, it turns brown and smells good. Why is this both physics AND chemistry?

choices.label: A) Only chemistry — the bread changes color.
B) Only physics — the heat travels into the bread.
C) Physics explains heat transfer (conduction), chemistry explains the Maillard reaction that browns the bread and creates flavor.
D) Neither — toasting is a mechanical process.

scenario.text: 💧 A barangay water pump lifts water from a deep well and treats it with chlorine. What combination of principles is used?

choices.label: A) Only physics — pumps move water.
B) Only chemistry — chlorine kills bacteria.
C) Physics of fluid pressure (Pascal's Principle) lifts the water, chemistry of chlorine disinfection makes it safe.
D) Neither — modern pumps use no science.

days.title: Formative Check — Escape the Synthesis Lab
days.content:
🔐 Formative Check — Escape the Synthesis Lab

You have 3 lives and 6 keys to unlock. You need 75% (5 of 6) to pass. Take your time — read every option carefully.

escape.text: Why do real-world systems often need both physics and chemistry to explain?

choices.label: A) Because both sciences are the same subject
B) Because most systems involve both energy/motion (physics) AND substance transformation (chemistry)
C) Because teachers require it
D) Because physics alone is too hard

escape.text: Inside a battery, what kind of chemical reaction produces electrical energy?

choices.label: A) Decomposition
B) Combustion
C) Redox (oxidation-reduction) reaction
D) Neutralization

escape.text: Which process in a car engine converts chemical energy into motion?

choices.label: A) Combustion of fuel → expanding gases push pistons → torque turns wheels
B) Evaporation of coolant
C) Refrigeration cycle
D) Electrolysis

escape.text: What chemistry process turns bread brown and flavorful when toasted?

choices.label: A) Photosynthesis
B) Maillard reaction
C) Neutralization
D) Fermentation

escape.text: An electric fan does NOT actually cool the air in a room. Why?

choices.label: A) Because it uses too much electricity.
B) Because it moves air (physics) which increases skin evaporation, making you feel cooler — but the air temperature stays the same.
C) Because it creates cold air from nothing.
D) Because it uses chemistry to cool air.

escape.text: Which of these is the BEST example of physics + chemistry working together?

choices.label: A) A bicycle bell ringing
B) A solar panel converting photons to electricity
C) A rice cooker heating water to cook rice — electrical resistance heats the coil, water boils, rice cooks
D) A cardboard box sitting on the floor
